Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

ahead adverb

of time: in advance, looking to the future

also plan ahead, think ahead, look ahead, ahead of time, for the future

classical

Cic. Fam. 2.8.1: ab homine longē in posterum prōspiciente
Ter. Ph. 781–782: plāgae crēscunt, nisi prōspicis

prōspiciō, prōspicere, prōspexī, prōspectum

verb, third conjugation (-iō)

look ahead, plan ahead, provide for what is coming

“To think far ahead” is longē in posterum prōspicere; with ut or nē, to see to it beforehand that … (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • in posterum — for the future, from now on

    adverbial phrase · also used · classical · Caes. BC 1.3.1: laudat prōmptōs atque in posterum cōnfirmat; Traupman 319

    Also “till the next day”, short for in posterum diem (Lewis & Short).

  • ante tempus — ahead of time, before the time; too soon

    also used · classical · Traupman 270, 394: ahead of time, ante tempus; Cic. Tusc. 1.93: ante tempus morī miserum esse

    Classically “before the proper time, too soon” (Lewis & Short); in good time is mātūrē (see early).

Examples

  • praesēns quod fuerat malum in diem abiit: plāgae crēscunt, nisi prōspicis

    the trouble that was here has only been put off: the beatings will pile up unless you think aheadTer. Ph. 781–782

  • sed ut ab homine longē in posterum prōspiciente futūra exspectō

    but from a man who looks far ahead I expect news of what is to comeCic. Fam. 2.8.1

See also ahead, early, future.

SourcesLewis & Short: prospicio · Lewis & Short: posterus · Lewis & Short: tempus
